title: Unit 8 L1: Regret & Forgiveness
source: Henry's Unit 8 lesson packs (M.3 Communication), Nov 13. American spelling (apologize, not the British -ise).

questions.q: Ava's friend needed her, but she stayed home to babysit. Ava says: "I really regret ___ you down."
questions.read_aloud: I really regret letting you down.

questions.q: Sasha called a classmate a bad name. She talks to her teacher, so she needs a formal phrase. What does she say?
choices: I apologize for calling Ben that name.
Sorry, I feel awful about Ben.
I wish I didn't call Ben that.
questions.read_aloud: I apologize for calling Ben that name.

questions.q: Ruth dropped Luis's tablet by accident, and Luis shouted at her. Now he says: "I'm sorry, I ___ have shouted at you like that."
questions.read_aloud: I'm sorry, I shouldn't have shouted at you like that.

questions.q: Tom wants Ava to know she did nothing wrong. Which phrase expresses forgiveness?
Nora told Emma a secret about Ellie's parents. Now she feels regret. She says: "I wish I ___ told Emma."
questions.read_aloud: I wish I hadn't told Emma.

questions.q: Luis feels bad about his angry words. He says: "I'm really sorry for ___ you."
questions.read_aloud: I'm really sorry for upsetting you.

questions.q: Sasha promises the teacher she won't do it again. What does she say?
choices: It won't happen again, I promise.
It wasn't my fault, I promise.
Don't worry about it, I promise.
questions.read_aloud: It won't happen again, I promise.

questions.q: Which forgiveness phrase means "It was not your choice. You had no control"?
Your best friend forgot your birthday and says sorry. You want to forgive them in an informal way. What do you say?
A friend says: "I really regret letting you down." How does your friend feel?
questions.read_aloud: I really regret letting you down.

scramble.text: I wish I hadn't told her.
I'm sorry if I upset you.
I feel really bad about it.
I shouldn't have shouted at you.
I'm really sorry for upsetting you.
I apologize for calling him a name.
It won't happen again, I promise.
